pr.title: Feed HIR for by-move coroutine body def, since the inliner tries to read its attrs
pr.description:
See the comments in the test. 

I'm surprised that nobody found this[^1] (edit: nvm haha), but you have to go out of your way to construct the by-move body and then inline it w/ a poll call, so I guess the inliner just never really gets into this situation before.

Fixes #134335

r? oli-obk

[^1]: Well, @eholk found this when working on the `iter! {}` macro, since it more dramatically affects those.

classification.name: StateTransform
evidence: implementation: compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/coroutine/by_move_body.rs

processing.reason: PR #139193 is an ICE fix in the compiler, not a miscompilation that changes runtime values. The pre-fix code creates a synthetic by-move coroutine body local DefId with `tcx.create_def` and omits `body_def.feed_hir()`; later the MIR inliner reads the body's attributes, `local_def_id_to_hir_id` is queried for the HIR-less synthetic def, and rustc panics with `index out of bounds`. The fix simply inserts `body_def.feed_hir()` before inheriting codegen/coverage attrs. There is no source-level original-vs-transformed function pair with differing concrete values: the user program (async closure through `call_once` then `.poll(...)`) has identical runtime semantics before and after the fix, because the only difference is whether compilation ICEs. Any function pair producing different numeric/boolean/character values would be an unrelated fabricated rewrite rather than the historical wrong transformation, which the task prohibits. Therefore no valid Miri-checked counterexample pair exists for this PR.

analysis.originalLogic: The by-move body query in `compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/coroutine/by_move_body.rs` synthesizes a by-move coroutine body `body_def` for an async closure's child coroutine, then copies attributes from the by-ref coroutine via `body_def.codegen_fn_attrs(tcx.codegen_fn_attrs(coroutine_def_id).clone());` and `body_def.coverage_attr_on(tcx.coverage_attr_on(coroutine_def_id));`. In the pre-fix revision, this synthetic local def was created without feeding HIR for it.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historical revision left the synthetic by-move coroutine body def without HIR while still treating it as a local def. When the MIR inliner later performs inlinability checks and reads the body's attributes (including checking for `#[rustc_no_mir_inline]`), the attribute query reaches `local_def_id_to_hir_id` for a def with no HIR slot and panics with `index out of bounds: the len is 12 but the index is 13`. The fix inserts `body_def.feed_hir();` immediately before the inherited attribute assignments, with the comment `// Feed HIR because we try to access this body's attrs in the inliner.`
analysis.inputDomain: Rust programs using edition-2024 async closures (for example `let x = async || {};`) where an async closure is passed to an inlined `FnOnce` helper such as `call_once`, producing the "FnOnce" flavor future whose synthetic by-move coroutine body is then inlined into a subsequent `.poll(...)` call, with MIR inlining enabled (e.g. `-Zinline-mir`).
analysis.summary: Bug-fix PR: the by-move coroutine body query (StateTransform) synthesized a local def for an async closure's by-move body but did not feed HIR; when the inliner inlined that synthetic body into a poll call and read its attrs, `local_def_id_to_hir_id` indexed out of bounds and ICEd. The fix calls `body_def.feed_hir()` before copying inherited attrs.
analysis.trigger: The inliner inlines the synthetic by-move coroutine body (the "FnOnce" flavor of an async closure's child coroutine) into a `poll` call and runs inlinability checks that read the body's attributes, causing `has_attr`/`local_def_id_to_hir_id` to be queried for a synthetic local def that has no HIR.
preconditions: Edition 2024 async closure is constructed (e.g. `let x = async || {};`).
A `call_once`-style `FnOnce` helper is inlined first, yielding a future whose type is the FnOnce flavor of the async closure's child coroutine.
The synthetic by-move coroutine body is produced by the by-move body query as a local def without HIR.
That body is then inlined into a subsequent `poll` call while MIR inlining is enabled (e.g. `-Zinline-mir`).
pitfalls: A local `DefId` does not imply HIR exists: synthetic defs created by the by-move body query have no HIR until explicitly fed.
Attribute lookups (e.g. `has_attr`/`#[rustc_no_mir_inline]` and inherited codegen/coverage attrs) require HIR; feed HIR before any attr access on the synthetic body.
Reproduction requires going out of the way to construct the by-move body and then inline it with a poll call; ordinary async fns may not exercise this path.
This is an ICE/panic involving HIR/attr queries, not a borrow-checking or post-copy overwrite issue; do not conflate the conditions.
analysis.testStrategy: Replace the `tests/crashes/134335.rs` known-bug test with a UI `check-pass` test under `tests/ui/async-await/async-closures/` compiled with `-Zinline-mir -Zvalidate-mir` and `//@ edition: 2024`. Construct an async closure (`let x = async || {};`), wrap it through an inlined `call_once` helper, then `pin!` it and call `fut.poll(&mut Context::from_waker(Waker::noop()))` so both the `call_once` inline and the poll-call inline of the synthetic by-move body occur, exercising the inliner's attr read. No compiler was built and the test was not executed here; the test is expected to compile without ICE after the fix.
